scope: Theorem 11.6 (Forward marker theorem) of the manuscript “Finite congruence lattices: characterization and undecidability” (preprints/Finite-Congruence-Lattices-Characterization-and-Undecidability-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 206 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d26d6cd6285de4f2), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 87. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every nonnegative integer m, there are integers a(m) and t0(m) such that the following holds whenever |T| ≥ t0(m). Every exact forward realization FT = [P, Sb ]∆ with S nonabelian simple, ∆ transitive on the factors, and invariant coordinate product P ̸= 1 (or b = 1), has the following configuration in the ordinary site interval of Lemma 11.5. There is A ⊂ T with |A| ≤ a(m) such that KMA has an actual high-degree alternating simple normal subgroup BA ≤ S satisfying HBA = KMA , CKMA (BA) ≤ H, CKMA (BA) is soluble. In the almost simple quotient KMA /CKMA (BA), at least m distinct labels MA∪{i}, with fresh indices i ∈ T \ A, are full stabilizers of individual points in the natural alternating action. The constants a(m) and t0(m) are independent of S, b, ∆, P and the realization; the high-degree threshold is the fixed one used in the structural exclusions.
